bottleneck: KV-pool capacity, not attention arithmetic, is the new candidate bottleneck for the two frozen points that never fit: PrefillHeavy C16 (16 x 8192 prompt tokens = 131072 = --max-total-tokens exactly, zero decode headroom, yet 512 decode tokens required) and DecodeCeiling C256 (256 x 544 = 139264, over capacity by 8192 from output token 481). Source anchors show the only pressure valve under --disable-radix-cache is retract_decode() -> re-queue/re-prefill, with an observable counter and '#retracted_reqs:' log line. This is the first full-engine hypothesis in this branch that is not on the saturated decode-roofline / host-sync / GGUF-unreachable lanes, and it targets the 15% PrefillHeavy point (branch-recorded 59.3 tok/s, ~4046 ms TTFT) and the 20% DecodeCeiling point. It is currently ARITHMETIC + SOURCE only; runtime causality is NOT established.
hypothesis: H1 (executed, arithmetic): under the frozen launch the per-point demand arithmetic over-commits the 131072-token full-attention KV pool at exactly two points, PrefillHeavy C16 (by 512 tokens at max output, prompt-only demand equal to the pool) and DecodeCeiling C256 (by 8192 tokens). H2 (not yet tested, falsifiable from existing artifacts): the PrefillHeavy point therefore spends decode time in retract/re-prefill churn - chunked prefill greedily refills space freed by a retraction, starving the next decode step - so its 59.3 tok/s is capacity-scheduling dominated rather than attention-bound. H3 (not yet tested): DecodeCeiling retraction, if present, occurs only after output token 480. Negative controls: short/medium/standard/decode_heavy all have max demand <= 98304 and should show ~0 retractions; nonzero there falsifies the capacity reading. H1 is NOT a throughput claim and does not by itself justify an engine patch.

learning: Executed facts: (a) the frozen workload's PrefillHeavy point is constructed so that its prompt tokens exactly equal the KV pool (16 x 8192 = 131072 = --max-total-tokens), leaving exactly zero headroom for its 32 output tokens per request; with --disable-radix-cache the source-anchored consequence is that retract_decode() is the only pressure release, and SGLang exposes both a counter (num_retracted_reqs) and a '#retracted_reqs:' log line; (b) DecodeCeiling C256 over-commits by 8192 tokens (6.25%) beginning at output token 481; (c) every other frozen point fits at max output (largest is decode_heavy C128 at 98304, 74.8% of pool). These are arithmetic + source anchors, not measurements: the new_token_ratio reservation, chunked-prefill admission policy, hybrid full-vs-SWA allocator binding, and possible EOS truncation are all unmodeled, and the 59.3 tok/s / 4046 ms baselines are branch-recorded history rather than re-measured here.
